title: A crossing is evidence a gate reads, so nothing may write one but the act of crossing
question: CC proposed that `emit` stamp the ticket's `crossings` array, because clearance-adjacent checks refuse PROVED without one and CC had been typing them by hand (196 of 230 tickets past PROVEME carry none; dd8ad9702b49's six were transcribed by CC on 2026-09-10). Is a new writer of that array allowed?
ruling: No. Akien, 2026-09-10: 'sounds like a no ... emit cannot create crossings, only a deterministic gate or explicit from me.' The proposal is refused and replaced: the array is DERIVED from history.json, never written anywhere.
what_gate_evidence_means: The facts a gate READS to decide - its inputs, not its verdict. Measured 2026-09-10, `crossings` is gate evidence in three places: proof_coverage.lacks() walks it for `proven_by` to decide whether a boat is COVERED (and clearance refuses PROVED on an uncovered boat); hollow.py walks it for the latest `to: BUILDME` entry to decide which commit the hollow reading reverts to; codemother/shim.py walks it for `proven_by`. A hand typing the array hands three gates their inputs.
why_the_replacement_is_not_a_writer: Every field `crossings` carries is already in history.json, written by `emit` at the instant the gates fired and refused before anything landed. Measured over the corpus: 566 journal entries carry at/seq/standing, 482 carry ticket, 467 carry from/to/direction, 187 carry proven_by.
So the ticket's array is a hand-maintained SECOND COPY of facts physics already recorded. Deriving it is a READ of the record of truth (Law 7), not a new write.

A gate must not write its own input. If emit stamped the array and proof_coverage read it to decide coverage, the loop closes and a bug in the stamp is invisible to every check downstream. Derivation keeps emit blind to the ticket.
hollow._buildme_at() ALREADY prefers the journal's `at` over the ticket's crossings[].date, falling back only when the journal is silent - the derivation pattern is proven and half-shipped.
Law 1: a settled fact stops being re-derived by a hand 196 times.
It makes the rule physics rather than vigilance: there is no way to write a crossing except by crossing, because there is no field left to type one into.
corrects: The tier-1 close report of 2026-09-10 said '196 tickets past PROVEME carry no crossings'. The crossings are not missing - the facts are in the journals; the duplicate is missing. No backfill is owed.
known_gap: A ticket's crossings span both ends of a seam, so the derivation scans history.json for entries carrying that ticket id. 566 entries corpus-wide; the cost is negligible.
traces_to: Law 7 (history.json is the record of truth)
